The Longsword deals 1d8 slashing damage, is versatile (1d10), can sap, weighs 3 lb., and costs 15 GP.
The Maul deals 2d6 bludgeoning damage, is heavy, two-handed, can topple, weighs 10 lb., and costs 10 GP.
The Morningstar deals 1d8 piercing damage and can sap, weighs 4 lb., and costs 15 GP.
The Pike deals 1d10 piercing damage, is heavy, has reach, is two-handed, can push, weighs 18 lb., and costs 5 GP.

parent:8a49bdf5230bcdfe2d0bd92189c8e97ae.title: Young Black Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8a49bdf5230bcdfe2d0bd92189c8e97ae.summary: The Young Black Dragon is a large, chaotic evil chromatic dragon with AC 18, initiative +5, 127 HP, and speeds of 40 ft. on land, 80 ft. flying, and 40 ft. swimming; it has perception and stealth skills, immunity to acid, blindsight and darkvision senses, and speaks Common and Draconic; its amphibious trait allows it to breathe air and water, and it can attack with a multiattack of three rends, a rend that deals slashing and acid damage, and an acid breath attack with a DC 14 saving throw causing 49 acid damage on a failed save or half damage on a successful save, recharging in 5-6 rounds.

parent:f536b7850adc20b43f604b008f6a2d0d1.title: Earth Elemental Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f536b7850adc20b43f604b008f6a2d0d1.summary: The Earth Elemental is a large, neutral elemental with AC 17, initiative -1, 147 HP, and speeds of 30 ft. and burrowing 30 ft., vulnerable to thunder but immune to various conditions, possessing darkvision, tremorsense, and speaking Primordial, with a CR of 5, capable of burrowing without disturbance, dealing double damage to objects and structures, and attacking with Slam and Rock Launch, the latter of which can knock smaller creatures prone.

parent:3e88eb4447b223fb41923de8e2a448d2d.title: Invisible Stalker Core Rules and Concepts
parent:3e88eb4447b223fb41923de8e2a448d2d.summary: The Invisible Stalker is a large, neutral elemental with invisibility, air form, and resistances to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, capable of entering tight spaces and attacking with Wind Swipe or using Vortex to grapple and damage opponents.

parent:2d7bef8d592d31b38c65d55cec33e7b56.title: Glabrezu Core Rules and Concepts
parent:2d7bef8d592d31b38c65d55cec33e7b56.summary: The Glabrezu is a large, chaotic evil demon with high AC, initiative, and HP, possessing resistances to cold, fire, and lightning, and immunities to poison, with truesight, telepathy, and skills in deception and perception; it can restore itself if killed outside the Abyss, has magic resistance, and uses multiattacks and spellcasting.

parent:10802de72d813e4499c963cf8423b4a89.title: Adult Silver Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:10802de72d813e4499c963cf8423b4a89.summary: The Adult Silver Dragon is a large, lawful good metallic dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, possessing legendary resistance, multiattack capabilities, cold breath and paralyzing breath attacks, spellcasting abilities, and legendary actions like chill, cold gale, and pounce.

parent:3e3da9f842c6d2a6afc991090b59f0eea.title: Hunter Shark Core Rules and Concepts
parent:3e3da9f842c6d2a6afc991090b59f0eea.summary: The Hunter Shark is a large, unaligned aquatic beast with a combat focus, characterized by its decent AC, high initiative, significant HP, and powerful bite attack, enhanced by blindsight for underwater detection, and restricted to underwater environments by its water breathing trait.

parent:323e271ab934b691adf6714c27fc85b77.title: Giant Ape Core Rules and Concepts
parent:323e271ab934b691adf6714c27fc85b77.summary: The Giant Ape is a formidable creature with high initiative and health, skilled in Athletics, capable of making powerful fist attacks and hurling boulders that can knock down smaller creatures, and can leap long distances as a bonus action.

parent:0df66a8dbce014b4945bb1947a868de4b.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:0df66a8dbce014b4945bb1947a868de4b.summary: The Incapacitated condition renders a character inactive, unable to concentrate or speak, and at a disadvantage on Initiative rolls; creatures are indifferent by default, requiring Influence checks to alter their behavior, while Initiative scores determine turn order in combat, and the Invisible condition grants advantage on Initiative rolls and concealment from effects.

parent:bf206766698fb7d0495d07f979a533a71.title: Rhythm of Play in D&D
parent:bf206766698fb7d0495d07f979a533a71.summary: D&D play revolves around a cyclical pattern where the GM describes the scene, players describe their characters' actions, and the GM narrates the results, with structured turns during combat.

parent:b3a2fbc9fa49564403813106129b3c57e.title: Swarm of Rats
parent:b3a2fbc9fa49564403813106129b3c57e.summary: The Swarm of Rats is a medium swarm of tiny beasts with AC 10, 14 HP, speed of 30 ft., resistances to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing, immunities to various conditions, darkvision, and a bite attack that deals 5 or 2 piercing damage, capable of occupying spaces and moving through small openings.

parent:6bfcd748af851f1af7847fa52e86a6c5d.title: D&D Spell Rules and Concepts
parent:6bfcd748af851f1af7847fa52e86a6c5d.summary: The snippet describes spells with varying effects, such as Bless enhancing attack rolls, Blight dealing necrotic damage, Blindness/Deafness imposing conditions, Blink allowing plane travel, Blur granting disadvantage on attacks, and Burning Hands causing fire damage, along with rules for using higher-level spell slots to enhance these effects.

parent:b540ab265faa06342450a95e56f380a18.title: Horned Devil Summary
parent:b540ab265faa06342450a95e56f380a18.summary: The Horned Devil is a large, lawful evil fiend with high AC, initiative, and HP, capable of flying, possessing resistances and immunities, and having darkvision and telepathy; it can revive in the Nine Hells upon death, has an advantage on saving throws against magic, and uses attacks like Searing Fork, Hurl Flame, and Infernal Tail to deal damage and inflict infernal wounds.

parent:13becbadd6fc0b9be6ae287bd95880277.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:13becbadd6fc0b9be6ae287bd95880277.summary: The snippet outlines the functionalities and conditions for using various D&D items, including a Rope for binding creatures, a Sack for carrying, a Scholar’s Pack with essential items, a Shovel for digging, a Signal Whistle for sound production, Spell Scrolls for casting spells, Iron Spikes for securing objects, a Spyglass for magnification, String for tying, a Tent for shelter, a Tinderbox for fire starting, a Torch for lighting and attacking, a Vial for holding liquids, and a Waterskin for hydration.

table:5274cf5ce07078c1885d62653fdcdb1b30.summary: The table lists magical items including a rope that imposes the Restrained condition, a sack with a specific capacity, and a scholar's pack with a given cost.
prose_rows: A bound creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes, which requires a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.
A Sack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot and costs 1 CP.
A Scholar’s Pack costs 40 GP.

table:0dcdbf413bf8d7dc709b1f924f14d773bf.summary: The table lists the items in a Scholar's Pack, including a Backpack, Book, Ink, Ink Pen, Lamp, 10 flasks of Oil, 10 sheets of Parchment, and a Tinderbox, and separately mentions a Shovel priced at 2 GP.
prose_rows: A Scholar’s Pack contains a Backpack, a Book, Ink, an Ink Pen, a Lamp, 10 flasks of Oil, 10 sheets of Parchment, and a Tinderbox.
A Shovel is available for 2 Gold Pieces (GP).

table:1264e394963be4e2fd338d8ff524523830.summary: The table lists the productivity of using a Shovel for one hour to dig a 5x5x5 feet hole in soil or similar material and mentions a Signal Whistle costing 5 CP.
prose_rows: Working for one hour, you can use a Shovel to dig a hole that is 5 feet on each side in soil or similar material, and you can also use a Signal Whistle which costs 5 CP.

table:7edcd03e7eb9f3c9fcba4f52306cbbd277.summary: The table lists a signal whistle that can be heard up to 600 feet away and provides the cost of its spell scroll as a cantrip for 30 GP and as a level 1 spell for 50 GP.
prose_rows: When blown as a Utilize action, a Signal Whistle produces a sound that can be heard up to 600 feet away.
A Spell Scroll for a Cantrip costs 30 GP.
A Level 1 Spell Scroll costs 50 GP.

table:3842e26bc78a62aa41b8feca8e04556893.summary: The table lists a magical scroll for the 'Spikes, Iron' spell, priced at 1 GP, with a spell save DC of 13, an attack bonus of +5, and it disintegrates after casting.
prose_rows: When casting the Iron Spikes spell, the spell save DC is 13, the attack bonus is +5, and the scroll disintegrates upon completion of the casting, costing 1 GP.

table:4ec6d59b0bedb03b1aa92e2f68bd753b05.summary: The table describes a hammer for driving spikes and a spyglass valued at 1,000 GP.
prose_rows: A hammer is used to drive a spike into wood, earth, or similar materials, which can be used to jam a door shut or to attach a Rope or Chain to the Spike, and a Spyglass is available for 1,000 GP.

table:22adee11108701ea25b590a77461f54510.summary: The table lists a String that is 10 feet long and can be knotted, a Tent that sleeps up to two Small or Medium creatures, and a Tinderbox, with their respective costs in SP or GP.
prose_rows: Objects viewed through a Spyglass are magnified to twice their size.
A String, costing 1 SP, is 10 feet long and can be tied into a knot as a Utilize action.
A Tent, priced at 2 GP, can sleep up to two Small or Medium creatures.
A Tinderbox, costing 5 SP, is a useful item in the game.

table:dc7c64a6874f5ae6ae45e18580368383f7.summary: The table specifies that lighting a torch requires a Bonus Action and costs 1 CP, whereas lighting other fires takes 1 minute.
prose_rows: A Lamp, Lantern, or Torch—or any item with exposed fuel—can be lit using a Bonus Action.
Lighting any other type of fire requires 1 minute.
A Torch costs 1 CP.

table:8bb108c381e574d099831c89e23fec60e8.summary: The table lists a Torch that can be used as a melee weapon causing fire damage and a Vial that holds up to 4 ounces, with their respective costs of 1 GP and 2 SP.
prose_rows: When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon, and on a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.
A Vial holds up to 4 ounces and costs 1 GP.
A Waterskin costs 2 SP.

parent:55eac04a3fe98d6834f48dacdea6c60b8.title: D&D Spell Summary
parent:55eac04a3fe98d6834f48dacdea6c60b8.summary: Dancing Lights creates movable light sources, Darkness generates impenetrable darkness, Darkvision grants dark sight, Daylight produces bright light, and Death Ward protects a creature from dying.

parent:63de8644b53ccfe0ca86c8142af487d99.title: Shield Guardian Core Rules and Concepts
parent:63de8644b53ccfe0ca86c8142af487d99.summary: The Shield Guardian is a Large Construct bound to an amulet, capable of transferring damage to itself, regenerating HP, storing and casting spells, and providing a defensive bonus to the amulet's wearer when attacked nearby.

parent:987d851ea505913b84ac1d3ce363da647.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:987d851ea505913b84ac1d3ce363da647.summary: The wall spell creates a moving barrier that deals damage and reduces in height each turn, Unseen Servant conjures a mindless force for simple tasks, and Vampiric Touch allows a caster to deal damage to a target and heal themselves.

parent:c2f471342d37650372b2da90b6e1af3fc.title: Efreeti Core Rules and Concepts
parent:c2f471342d37650372b2da90b6e1af3fc.summary: Efreeti are large, fire-immune genies with high AC and HP, capable of elemental restoration, magic resistance, and casting spells like 'Wish' under specific conditions, and they attack with heated blades and hurl flames, while also possessing spellcasting abilities.

parent:6e03a19df9822dcc73625e77c64dca9fe.title: Hyena Core Rules and Concepts
parent:6e03a19df9822dcc73625e77c64dca9fe.summary: The hyena is a medium beast with an AC of 11, initiative +1, 5 HP, and a speed of 50 ft., possessing darkvision and a Perception skill of +3; it uses pack tactics for advantage in combat and can bite for 3 piercing damage, with a challenge rating of 0.

parent:2b32d78b06f1754eb9855e57b69b77486.title: Iron Golem Core Rules and Concepts
parent:2b32d78b06f1754eb9855e57b69b77486.summary: The Iron Golem is a large, unaligned construct with high AC, initiative, and HP, immune to fire, poison, psychic, and several conditions, possessing darkvision and understanding multiple languages, featuring Fire Absorption, Immutable Form, and Magic Resistance, and capable of Multiattack, Bladed Arm, Fiery Bolt, and Poison Breath.

parent:c2c7014e89a10169d1332fcfb65b2600a.title: Ancient Silver Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:c2c7014e89a10169d1332fcfb65b2600a.summary: The Ancient Silver Dragon is a formidable Lawful Good dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, excelling in History and Perception, immune to cold, and capable of powerful attacks like Rend and Paralyzing Breath, along with spellcasting abilities and Legendary Actions.

parent:91343cf448efd9684f9423cfba46477dd.title: Gladiator Character Summary
parent:91343cf448efd9684f9423cfba46477dd.summary: The Gladiator is a Medium or Small Humanoid with high AC and initiative, skilled in Athletics, equipped with a shield, spears, and studded leather armor, capable of multiattacks with spears or shield bash, and can parry melee attacks to increase AC.

parent:f9d455bdd9a354d076f18d234c5d73a7f.title: Swarm of Ravens Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f9d455bdd9a354d076f18d234c5d73a7f.summary: The Swarm of Ravens is a medium swarm of tiny, unaligned beasts with resistances to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, immunities to various conditions, and abilities to occupy spaces, move through small openings, attack with beaks causing piercing damage, and use cacophony to deafen targets, imposing disadvantages on their actions.

parent:74754a453c237bbc8e577df6bcaee5dc1.title: D&D Rulebook Spell Summary
parent:74754a453c237bbc8e577df6bcaee5dc1.summary: The 'Freedom of Movement' spell grants a creature immunity to difficult terrain and magical speed reduction, along with a Swim Speed and escape from nonmagical restraints, while 'Freezing Sphere' creates a damaging ice explosion and can be stored for later use, and 'Gaseous Form' transforms a creature into a misty cloud with limited movement.

table:ff3185412d273de2c335d1f6dea50ee9d2.summary: The table lists a Level 9 Conjuration spell with an action casting time, a range of 60 feet, and components including verbal, somatic, and a diamond worth 5,000+ GP.
prose_rows: The level 9 Conjuration spell, available to Clerics, Sorcerers, Warlocks, and Wizards, requires an action to cast, has a range of 60 feet, and necessitates verbal, somatic components, and a diamond worth at least 5,000 GP as material components.

parent:2290ac7b10dc14aed8bd530183f0efc12.title: Hydra Core Rules and Concepts
parent:2290ac7b10dc14aed8bd530183f0efc12.summary: The Hydra is a large, unaligned monstrosity with high AC and initiative, capable of swimming and possessing darkvision, immune to several conditions, and can regenerate heads and HP after taking significant damage, except from fire, while each head provides additional reactions for opportunity attacks.

parent:a55804f5470c1413dbb4da780612e8454.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:a55804f5470c1413dbb4da780612e8454.summary: The snippet outlines the mechanics of a pressure plate trap, various items like ink, pens, jugs, ladders, lamps, lanterns, locks, magnifying glasses, manacles, maps, and their specific uses, costs, and interactions within the game.

table:91f1480eabdda83b786a5af1068dc7f79e.summary: The table lists a magical item called 'Ink' that costs 10 GP and enables a Strength (Athletics) check to free a creature, with failed attempts causing 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature.
prose_rows: Performing a Strength (Athletics) check allows a creature to free itself or another within reach on success, but each failed attempt deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature, costing 10 GP.

table:b8a47b4b7bcc258f491e021043e5877d29.summary: The table lists items including Ink, Ink Pen, Jug, and Ladder, detailing their capacities or uses and associated costs in CP or SP.
prose_rows: Ink comes in a 1-ounce bottle, which provides enough ink to write about 500 pages.
An Ink Pen, costing 2 CP, is used to write or draw using Ink.
A Jug, costing 2 CP, holds up to 1 gallon.
A Ladder, costing 1 SP, is available for use.

table:7b4a362295f0b4e187540decbe7a457b94.summary: The table lists a Lamp costing 5 SP that provides Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet, and a Lantern, Bullseye costing 10 GP.
prose_rows: A ladder is 10 feet tall, and you must climb it to move up or down.
A Lamp costs 5 SP and burns oil to cast bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
A Lantern, Bullseye costs 10 GP.

table:185c22289d593e30eea22124b8e44bb729.summary: The Bullseye Lantern, valued at 5 GP, burns oil to emit bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet.
prose_rows: The Hooded Lantern, costing 5 gold pieces, burns oil as fuel to cast bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet.

table:2f7fddb75e9c90c22bdc0341b5985f34eb.summary: The table lists a hood that emits light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet, with a bonus action to adjust the light to a 5-foot radius, and includes a lock feature valued at 10 GP.
prose_rows: The hood emits light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet, and as a bonus action, you can lower the hood to reduce the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius or raise it again, with the lock costing 10 gold pieces.

table:d82ada4a8d2a74330826c76e07cc3b9bff.summary: The table describes a lock that can be picked with Thieves’ Tools if the key is unavailable, requiring a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, and lists a Magnifying Glass priced at 100 GP.
prose_rows: A Magnifying Glass costs 100 GP and can be used to aid in tasks requiring detailed observation.

table:8162d251b1e169d031e55ed8ad28c4856b.summary: The table outlines the conditions needed to light a fire with a magnifying glass, requiring sunlight, tinder, and time, and also lists 'Manacles' valued at 2 GP.
prose_rows: To light a fire with a Magnifying Glass, you need sunlight-like brightness, tinder, and approximately 5 minutes for ignition. Manacles are available for 2 gold pieces.

table:bcabc71034a9f86db3abb99c622e2143b9.summary: The table outlines a lock-picking scenario using Thieves’ Tools with a DC 15 Dexterity check and notes a Map valued at 1 GP.
prose_rows: A creature can use Thieves’ Tools to pick the lock on manacles with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, and there is a map valued at 1 GP.

table:3011d707b9f813aacff15c3cc3134b177e.summary: The table lists magical items including a map that aids in navigation, a mirror useful for cosmetics and signaling, and a net priced at 1 GP.
prose_rows: Consulting an accurate map grants a +5 bonus to Wisdom (Survival) checks for navigation in the depicted area.
A handheld steel mirror, priced at 5 GP, is useful for personal cosmetics, peeking around corners, and reflecting light as a signal.
A net, priced at 1 GP, is listed as an item.

table:411af11f1094dd88d9ccccf3d47ac300c4.summary: The table outlines how a creature can be freed from a Net effect either by succeeding in a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check or by destroying the Net, which has AC 10, 5 HP, and immunities to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage.
prose_rows: The Oil spell creates a net with AC 10, 5 HP, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage. A restrained creature can be freed by making a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check or by destroying the net.

parent:b8f25f267dc8e742b549e1842d1d4e948.title: D&D Multiclassing Rules
parent:b8f25f267dc8e742b549e1842d1d4e948.summary: Multiclassing in D&D allows characters to gain levels in multiple classes, requiring specific ability scores, with experience points and hit points calculated based on total character level, and proficiency bonuses and class features acquired according to the combined levels across classes.

table:45f4da9a8fa1253ed27aacd975a7d9b915.summary: The table lists the starting level, equipment, money, and magic items for characters with Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher, detailing the resources and items available at different levels from 2 to 20.
prose_rows: Characters with Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher starting at levels 2 to 4 receive normal starting equipment and 1 Common magic item.
Characters with Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher starting at levels 5 to 10 receive normal starting equipment, 500 GP plus 1d10 × 25 GP, and 1 Common and 1 Uncommon magic item.

Characters with Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher starting at levels 11 to 16 receive normal starting equipment, 5,000 GP plus 1d10 × 250 GP, and 2 Common, 3 Uncommon, and 1 Rare magic items.

Characters with Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher starting at levels 17 to 20 receive normal starting equipment, 20,000 GP plus 1d10 × 250 GP, and 2 Common, 4 Uncommon, 3 Rare, and 1 Very Rare magic items.

parent:0c469dfde73c140c47169825dc17c6cb2.title: D&D Sorcerer Spells and Draconic Subclass Overview
parent:0c469dfde73c140c47169825dc17c6cb2.summary: The D&D rulebook snippet lists spells organized by level and school, with special notations, and describes the Draconic Sorcerer subclass, which grants increased hit points and a modified armor class based on Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

parent:bfcefd07fd9c43b804079117dd73b2643.title: Erinyes Core Rules and Concepts
parent:bfcefd07fd9c43b804079117dd73b2643.summary: The Erinyes is a Medium Fiend with high AC, initiative, and HP, featuring Diabolical Restoration, Magic Resistance, and a Magic Rope, excelling in combat with Multiattack and Withering Sword, and defensive Parry.

parent:8a199089e9d3aac6b8fa2cfb8ba3791f4.title: Jackal D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:8a199089e9d3aac6b8fa2cfb8ba3791f4.summary: The Jackal is a small, unaligned beast with AC 12, initiative +2, 3 HP, 40 ft. speed, Perception +5, Stealth +4, darkvision 90 ft., passive Perception 15, no languages, CR 0, and a bite attack dealing 1 piercing damage (1d4 – 1).

parent:c9c9f90dc96f4d2d106b1eb7ab913cdf4.title: Iron Golem Core Rules and Concepts
parent:c9c9f90dc96f4d2d106b1eb7ab913cdf4.summary: The Iron Golem is a neutral Medium or Small Humanoid with 52 HP, AC 18, and a speed of 30 ft., immune to being frightened, equipped with a greatsword, heavy crossbow, and plate armor, capable of multiattacks and a parry reaction, speaking Common plus one other language, with a challenge rating of 3.

parent:2ff4da165ac20c97002944855eb83d777.title: D&D Skeleton Rulebook Snippet
parent:2ff4da165ac20c97002944855eb83d777.summary: Skeletons are Medium Undead creatures with Lawful Evil alignment, possessing an AC of 14, initiative of +3, 13 HP, a speed of 30 ft., vulnerabilities to bludgeoning, immunities to poison and exhaustion, equipped with a shortbow and shortsword, darkvision of 60 ft., passive perception of 9, understanding of Common and one other language, a challenge rating of 1/4, and can attack with a shortsword or shortbow causing piercing damage.

parent:b2c7f729b0433bcbadd52f0e37a341cd3.title: Giant Hyena Core Rules
parent:b2c7f729b0433bcbadd52f0e37a341cd3.summary: The Giant Hyena is a large, unaligned beast with a base AC of 12, initiative +2, 45 HP, and a speed of 50 ft., capable of a bite attack dealing 10 piercing damage and a daily Rampage action to attack again after damaging a bloodied creature.

parent:b8833fa42358a17edd0ae50ae33acc160.title: Summary of D&D Spells: Gate, Geas, and Gentle Repose
parent:b8833fa42358a17edd0ae50ae33acc160.summary: The 'Gate' spell conjures a portal to another plane, allowing travel and potentially transporting a named creature, but can be blocked by deities; 'Geas' imposes a command on a creature, causing damage if disobeyed, and can be extended with higher-level slots; 'Gentle Repose' preserves a corpse from decay and undead transformation for ten days.

parent:eb22a38035b51582ea68c1a4be6f3a0b1.title: Ice Devil Core Rules and Concepts
parent:eb22a38035b51582ea68c1a4be6f3a0b1.summary: The Ice Devil is a large, Lawful Evil fiend with high AC, initiative, and HP, skilled in Insight, Perception, and Persuasion, immune to cold, fire, and poison, with blindsight and telepathy, capable of diabolical restoration and magic resistance, and can perform multiattacks with Ice Spear and Tail, and cast Ice Wall.

parent:53637b1cec215692d5095e994de48dc78.title: D&D Barbarian Rage and Combat Enhancements
parent:53637b1cec215692d5095e994de48dc78.summary: As a Barbarian progresses, they gain abilities to sustain Rage despite injuries, enhance combat effects like Brutal Strike, and ultimately increase their Strength and Constitution, embodying primal power.

parent:6507bc1bbfbe1dda0d56907129fa04b4b.title: D&D Weapons Core Rules Summary
parent:6507bc1bbfbe1dda0d56907129fa04b4b.summary: In D&D, weapons are categorized as Simple or Martial, classified as Melee or Ranged, and have specific damage, properties, and mastery requirements, with proficiency needed to add bonuses to attack rolls, and various properties like Ammunition, Finesse, Heavy, Light, and Loading affecting their use.

parent:948de9ebbd53bb0bbd1bccaaa0a637d4a.title: Ettercap Core Rules and Concepts
parent:948de9ebbd53bb0bbd1bccaaa0a637d4a.summary: The ettercap is a neutral evil monstrosity with abilities to climb, move through webs, and attack with biting and clawing, while also using web strands to restrain targets, which it can reel in as a bonus action.

parent:f94bbbdb293eeda30ad2d0862ac993273.title: Wereboar Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f94bbbdb293eeda30ad2d0862ac993273.summary: The Wereboar is a neutral evil lycanthrope with high AC and HP, capable of shape-shifting between humanoid, hybrid, and boar forms, attacking with javelins, tusks, or gore, and cursing humanoids with its gore attack, while moving faster in boar form and having a perception skill but unable to speak in boar form.

parent:af7dac7504125420e443a89f896e1ec70.title: Killer Whale D&D Rulebook Snippet
parent:af7dac7504125420e443a89f896e1ec70.summary: The Killer Whale is a Huge Beast with an AC of 12, initiative of +2, 90 HP, speeds of 5 ft. and 60 ft. swimming, Perception +3, Stealth +4, blindsight 120 ft., no languages, and a challenge rating of 3, capable of holding its breath for 30 minutes and delivering a 21 damage bite attack.

parent:f89c06688e3f993064524d0dec06c6b2b.title: Kobold Warrior Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f89c06688e3f993064524d0dec06c6b2b.summary: The Kobold Warrior, a small dragon with neutral alignment, has an AC of 14, 7 HP, and a speed of 30 ft., equipped with daggers and possessing darkvision; it uses pack tactics for combat advantage and suffers from sunlight sensitivity, with its main action being a dagger attack.

parent:179e5d36b516549a26efae9327feae608.title: Warhorse Skeleton Core Rules
parent:179e5d36b516549a26efae9327feae608.summary: The Warhorse Skeleton is a Large Undead with Lawful Evil alignment, vulnerable to bludgeoning, immune to poison and exhaustion, and can move 60 ft. per turn; it deals 7 bludgeoning damage with its hooves attack, potentially causing a target to become prone if it moved 20+ feet straight toward them before hitting.

parent:8c106904575e1f68f28d26dd96197cfe9.title: Giant Lizard Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8c106904575e1f68f28d26dd96197cfe9.summary: The Giant Lizard is a large, unaligned beast with an AC of 12, initiative +1, 19 HP, and can move and climb at 40 ft., possessing darkvision and a passive perception of 10; it has no language skills, a CR of 1/4, and can climb without checks, using a bite attack that deals 6 piercing damage.

parent:3f1ae81f79c00bbcbff7858d93be1a617.title: Imp Core Rules and Concepts
parent:3f1ae81f79c00bbcbff7858d93be1a617.summary: An Imp is a Tiny Fiend with Lawful Evil alignment, possessing high AC, initiative, and HP, along with resistances to cold and immunities to fire and poison, and it can use Magic Resistance, Sting, Invisibility, and Shape-Shift to adapt and attack in various forms.

parent:2125b08f13a50ce3b48c5fb52f76d6f86.title: Temporary Hit Points in D&D
parent:2125b08f13a50ce3b48c5fb52f76d6f86.summary: Temporary Hit Points are a separate pool from regular Hit Points, allowing a choice between keeping existing THP or gaining new ones, but not combining them, and they cannot be converted to Hit Points, restored by healing, or bring a creature back from unconsciousness.

parent:81a91b9ff3950f69787d13be707c16aa7.title: Shrieker Fungus Core Rules
parent:81a91b9ff3950f69787d13be707c16aa7.summary: The Shrieker Fungus is a medium plant with AC 5, initiative -5, 13 HP, 5 ft. speed, immunities to being blinded, charmed, deafened, or frightened, blindsight 30 ft., passive perception 6, no languages, CR 0, and a 'Shriek' reaction triggered by creatures or bright light within 30 feet, audible within 300 feet for 1 minute or until it dies.

parent:85fa531c2c6d5ca657324732e10110a69.title: Bone Devil Core Rules and Concepts
parent:85fa531c2c6d5ca657324732e10110a69.summary: The Bone Devil is a large, lawful evil fiend with high initiative and AC, notable for its resistances and immunities, including cold, fire, and poison, and skills in deception and insight; it can revive in the Nine Hells upon death, has magic resistance, and attacks with claws and an infernal sting that inflicts piercing and poison damage, preventing the target from regaining hit points while poisoned.

parent:cfa60b0fb726fdc474e203e9f35b03f0c.title: Wererat Core Rules and Concepts
parent:cfa60b0fb726fdc474e203e9f35b03f0c.summary: The wererat is a medium or small monstrosity with lawful evil alignment, capable of shape-shifting between humanoid, hybrid, and rat forms, and can curse humanoids with its bite attack, potentially transforming them into wererats under the GM's control.

parent:ee901b7f8490fb3acaa7b389009b78b13.title: Lion D&D Rulebook Summary
parent:ee901b7f8490fb3acaa7b389009b78b13.summary: The Lion is a Large Beast with AC 12, Initiative +2, 22 HP, and a speed of 50 ft., possessing darkvision and skills in Perception and Stealth; it uses Pack Tactics for attack advantages, can perform a Running Leap, and has actions including Multiattack, Rend, and Roar, which can frighten targets.

parent:596cda1be2221c5f9c328e7c2e5ae529f.title: Commoner Character Summary
parent:596cda1be2221c5f9c328e7c2e5ae529f.summary: A Commoner is a Medium or Small Humanoid with AC 10, Initiative +0, 4 HP, 30 ft. speed, and a club; it has a Passive Perception of 10, speaks Common, and a CR of 0; it gains proficiency in a GM-chosen skill with Advantage on checks, and can attack with a club for +2 attack roll and 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

parent:fe54015daff08d184d0eb26d3da545610.title: Kraken Core Rules and Concepts
parent:fe54015daff08d184d0eb26d3da545610.summary: The kraken is a gargantuan, chaotic evil monstrosity with high AC, initiative, and HP, capable of breathing air and water, possessing immunities and truesight, and understanding multiple languages. It has legendary resistance, deals double damage to objects, and can multiattack with tentacles, fling creatures, strike with lightning, and swallow creatures, which can be regurgitated if it takes significant damage, and it also has legendary actions like storm bolts and toxic ink.

parent:5837e12cd207c95d008863da3192acd63.title: Giant Octopus Core Rules and Concepts
parent:5837e12cd207c95d008863da3192acd63.summary: The Giant Octopus is a large, unaligned beast with AC 11, initiative +1, 45 HP, and speeds of 10 ft. on land and 60 ft. in water, possessing darkvision, no language skills, and a CR of 1; it can breathe underwater, grapple and restrain smaller creatures with its tentacles, and release an ink cloud to obscure vision when damaged.

parent:598e01342ba6dcd69692112c84f08277f.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:598e01342ba6dcd69692112c84f08277f.summary: The snippet outlines various D&D items, detailing their costs, functionalities, and specific actions or advantages, such as the Climber’s Kit for anchoring, the Diplomat’s Pack for travel, and the Costume for impersonation, among others.

table:a695e71319990dba92fc9a6a74124a60ef.summary: The table outlines a climbing rule limiting fall and movement distance from an anchor point and lists 'Clothes, Fine' valued at 15 GP.
prose_rows: The 'Clothes, Fine' item, valued at 15 gold pieces, allows a climber to fall no more than 25 feet from the anchor point and move no more than 25 feet from it without undoing the anchor as a Bonus Action.

table:cf9fe4e6e90b0cb78687a4455d51fcbc19.summary: The table lists 'Clothes, Traveler’s' priced at 2 GP, which are necessary for entry into specific events and locations due to their expertly crafted details.
prose_rows: The Clothes, Traveler’s, priced at 2 gold pieces, are adorned with expertly crafted details and are required for entry into some events and locations.

table:253562a0e935cb3b170b3f3b33cc7f5e80.summary: The table lists the Component Pouch, a resilient garment for travel priced at 25 GP.
prose_rows: The Component Pouch, a type of Traveler's Clothes designed for resilience in various environments, is valued at 25 GP.

table:fd1146262ae5dcb25edd588ccecd2d4915.summary: The table lists a watertight Component Pouch with compartments for spell components, costing 5 GP.
prose_rows: A Component Pouch is watertight and filled with compartments that hold all the free Material components of your spells, costing 5 gold pieces.

table:76a69601540ca93eeebec63880bfbe6548.summary: The table lists a 'Crowbar' costing 2 GP and notes that wearing a costume grants an advantage on impersonation ability checks.
prose_rows: While wearing a costume, you gain advantage on any ability check to impersonate the person or type of person it represents, and the Crowbar costs 2 gold pieces.

table:32852e3d9bb8dae3c5ceae656e93256c18.summary: The table indicates that using a Crowbar provides an advantage on Strength checks where leverage is applicable and lists the Diplomat’s Pack priced at 39 GP.
prose_rows: Using a Crowbar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Crowbar’s leverage can be applied.
The Diplomat’s Pack costs 39 GP.

table:31b1ff6ccd53f599f1e5e8cf51cc4b75a7.summary: The table lists Druidic Spellcasting Focuses, including a sprig of mistletoe, a wooden staff, and a yew wand, with their respective weights and costs, and mentions a Dungeoneer's Pack option.
prose_rows: A sprig of mistletoe can be used as a Druidic Focus and costs 1 GP.
A wooden staff, which can also serve as a Quarterstaff, weighs 4 lb and costs 5 GP.
A yew wand weighs 1 lb and costs 10 GP.
A Dungeoneer’s Pack costs 12 GP.

table:80404d0621ab451b89554165e1cf6573be.summary: The table lists an 'Entertainer’s Pack' valued at 40 GP, containing Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, 10 Torches, and Waterskin, with a reference to 'System Reference Document 5.2' and the number 97.
prose_rows: The Entertainer’s Pack, valued at 40 gold pieces, includes days of rations, rope, a tinderbox, 10 torches, and a waterskin.

table:c8aa667364fcc34bb6d869d8f7419d4c31.summary: The table lists the items in an Entertainer’s Pack, which includes a backpack, bedroll, bell, lantern, costumes, mirror, oil flasks, rations, tinderbox, and waterskin, and also mentions an Explorer’s Pack priced at 10 GP.
prose_rows: The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Backpack.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Bedroll.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Bell.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Bullseye Lantern.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes 3 Costumes.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Mirror.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes 8 flasks of Oil.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes 9 days of Rations.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Tinderbox.
The Entertainer’s Pack includes a Waterskin.

table:954521561c1f9a618f70a651ca12eea4d4.summary: The Explorer's Pack includes a Backpack, Bedroll, 2 flasks of Oil, 10 days of Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, 10 Torches, and Waterskin, with additional details that a Flask holds up to 1 pint and costs 2 CP, and a Grappling Hook costs 2 GP.
prose_rows: An Explorer’s Pack contains a Backpack, Bedroll, 2 flasks of Oil, 10 days of Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, 10 Torches, and a Waterskin.
A Flask holds up to 1 pint and costs 2 CP.
A Grappling Hook costs 2 GP.

table:f1e526152b50d4f88b18408f526c444760.summary: The table outlines a method for climbing using a hook and rope, contingent on a successful Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, and lists a Healer's Kit priced at 5 GP.
prose_rows: You can attempt to hook onto a railing, ledge, or similar object within 50 feet using a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check with a DC of 13. If successful and a rope is tied to the hook, you can climb. Additionally, there is a Healer's Kit available for 5 GP.

table:5292cabb5a706f2f01952bc8da558c89b0.summary: The table lists holy symbols including Amulet, Emblem, and Reliquary with their respective weights, costs, and methods of being worn or held, along with the cost of Holy Water.
prose_rows: An Amulet can be worn or held, weighs 1 lb., and costs 5 GP.
An Emblem can be borne on fabric or a Shield and costs 5 GP.
A Reliquary can be held, weighs 2 lb., and costs 5 GP.
Holy Water costs 25 GP.

table:461c72a131680f8f0f155d9b6a62320a6f.summary: The table lists a magical item, 'Hunting Trap' (5 GP), which targets a creature within 20 feet, requiring a Dexterity saving throw to avoid 2d8 Radiant damage, particularly affecting Fiends or Undead.
prose_rows: The Hunting Trap spell, costing 5 GP, targets a creature within 20 feet, requiring it to make a Dexterity saving throw with a DC of 8 plus the caster's Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus. If the target is a Fiend or Undead and fails the save, it takes 2d8 Radiant damage.

parent:5d48740436c0859a5d26f3d806e487d4b.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:5d48740436c0859a5d26f3d806e487d4b.summary: The spell causes a bead to explode on a failed Dexterity save or when touched, with damage increasing per turn and spell slot level, while 'Demiplane' creates a door to a new or existing demiplane, and 'Detect Evil and Good' and 'Detect Magic' sense specific entities or magical effects within a range, blocked by certain materials.

parent:bb8d18c6f32490d52812826bb0b2bc5b4.title: D&D Spell Summary
parent:bb8d18c6f32490d52812826bb0b2bc5b4.summary: The snippet outlines various spells from different schools of magic, detailing their casting times, ranges, components, durations, and effects, including saving throws, damage types, and unique conditions or transformations.

table:aaf0f83dc059738b8a92d78e126733b8dd.summary: The table lists the details of the 'Level 5 Necromancy (Druid)' spell, including its casting time of 1 hour, touch range, and components required, notably rare oils valued at over 1,000 GP.
prose_rows: The level 5 Necromancy spell for Druids has a casting time of 1 hour, a range of touch, and requires verbal, somatic, and material components, including rare oils worth over 1,000 gold pieces.

parent:2de247c57ccaf377d53984d5cf93e2186.title: D&D Creature Index Summary
parent:2de247c57ccaf377d53984d5cf93e2186.summary: The snippet provides a list of creatures from a D&D rulebook, each followed by a page number indicating where detailed information about them can be found.

parent:332278def3dd9b32d5e4d1989fd17eae0.title: Incubus Core Rules and Concepts
parent:332278def3dd9b32d5e4d1989fd17eae0.summary: The Incubus is a Medium Fiend with high AC and initiative, capable of shape-shifting into a Succubus, casting spells like Disguise Self and Dream, and using attacks such as Restless Touch to curse targets and Nightmare to inflict Psychic damage or unconsciousness.

parent:a359cf97c48ee688f4d3c60ff04cbdcb9.title: Violet Fungus Summary
parent:a359cf97c48ee688f4d3c60ff04cbdcb9.summary: The Violet Fungus is a medium, unaligned plant with AC 5, Initiative -5, 18 HP, 5 ft. speed, immunities to being blinded, charmed, deafened, or frightened, blindsight 30 ft., passive perception 6, no languages, CR 1/4, and can perform two Rotting Touch attacks dealing 4 necrotic damage each.

parent:907cda07a08bd49c234916181c13a7741.title: Paladin Class Features Summary
parent:907cda07a08bd49c234916181c13a7741.summary: Paladins start with two level 1 spells, increasing their prepared spells as they level up, use Charisma for spellcasting, and can use a Holy Symbol as a focus; they gain weapon mastery, a fighting style feat, always-prepared Divine Smite, and Channel Divinity abilities, with options to change prepared spells after a Long Rest.

parent:12a6b557734a957d893ec83385538da5a.title: Brass Dragon Wyrmling Core Rules and Concepts
parent:12a6b557734a957d893ec83385538da5a.summary: The Brass Dragon Wyrmling is a Medium-sized, Chaotic Good Metallic Dragon with an Armor Class of 15, Initiative of +2, 22 Hit Points, and speeds of 30 ft., 15 ft. burrowing, and 60 ft. flying; it has immunities to fire, skills in Perception and Stealth, senses including blindsight and darkvision, and speaks Draconic; its actions include a melee attack with a reach of 5 ft., a fire breath with a recharge time of 5-6 rounds, and a sleep breath with specific saving throw mechanics, all contributing to its challenge rating of 1.

parent:48df5f75713cb6dc19a2e07139e4750ba.title: Weretiger Core Rules and Concepts
parent:48df5f75713cb6dc19a2e07139e4750ba.summary: The Weretiger is a neutral-aligned lycanthrope with abilities to attack using Bite, Scratch, or Longbow, shape-shift between humanoid and tiger forms, and use a Prowl action for stealthy movement, with a curse effect on humanoid targets hit by its Bite attack.

parent:dd8c8d85d3da0dd9d4d489fb02dd2104c.title: Copper Dragon Wyrmling Core Rules
parent:dd8c8d85d3da0dd9d4d489fb02dd2104c.summary: The Copper Dragon Wyrmling is a Medium, Chaotic Good dragon with AC 16, 22 HP, and various movement abilities, possessing skills in Perception and Stealth, immunity to acid, and breath attacks that include Acid Breath and Slowing Breath, along with a Rend melee attack.

parent:bb4c98e043eb7c6a3675f827077cb8a65.title: Core Rules and Concepts in D&D Rulebook Snippet
parent:bb4c98e043eb7c6a3675f827077cb8a65.summary: The snippet details task difficulty levels, saving throws with ability modifiers and proficiency bonuses, attack rolls with ability modifiers and proficiency bonuses, and the concept of Armor Class in D&D.

parent:8acb07531ad526e211ac5d2fc52583850.title: Lizard Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8acb07531ad526e211ac5d2fc52583850.summary: The Lizard is a Tiny Beast with AC 10, 2 HP, and a +0 initiative, capable of climbing difficult surfaces without checks, and it attacks with a bite dealing 1 piercing damage.

parent:5681f0f9c23fe232dcd2ba5bd6109a0eb.title: Giant Owl Core Rules and Concepts
parent:5681f0f9c23fe232dcd2ba5bd6109a0eb.summary: The Giant Owl is a large celestial creature with a balanced AC and initiative, moderate HP, and the ability to fly and move stealthily, possessing resistances to necrotic and radiant damage, darkvision, and the ability to cast spells like Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, and Clairvoyance, while also having a melee attack with its talons.

parent:0224c91f95dfde2ec33a5b262ee0e830a.title: D&D Spell Descriptions
parent:0224c91f95dfde2ec33a5b262ee0e830a.summary: The 'Sense Thoughts' spell detects thinking creatures within 30 feet, while 'Read Thoughts' allows probing into a creature's mind, with resistance and awareness mechanics. 'Dimension Door' enables instant teleportation to a specified location or a willing creature, with damage if obstructed. 'Disguise Self' alters appearance, detectable by physical inspection.

parent:bb6af5aa23ce9d633931dd6b10ed229cc.title: D&D Rulebook Spell Summary
parent:bb6af5aa23ce9d633931dd6b10ed229cc.summary: The barrier spell creates an impenetrable sphere immune to damage, allowing movement within; the resistance spell reduces damage from a chosen type; resurrection spells revive dead creatures with varying conditions and penalties; and the Reverse Gravity spell alters gravity within a specified area, causing upward falls.

table:b22677e184adef97ca38b2239d015ab3cd.summary: The table lists the details of the 'Level 7 Necromancy' spell, including its casting time, range, and components, specifically noting a diamond worth 1,000+ GP as a material component.
prose_rows: The level 7 Necromancy spell, available to Bards and Clerics, requires a casting time of 1 hour, has a touch range, and necessitates verbal, somatic, and material components, including a diamond worth at least 1,000 gold pieces.

table:7de818257378bac8afb0fc1f2f04dd7404.summary: The table lists a Level 3 Necromancy spell for Clerics, Druids, Paladins, and Rangers, with an action casting time, touch range, and components including verbal, somatic components, and a diamond worth 300+ GP.
prose_rows: The Level 3 Necromancy spell can be cast as an action, requires touching the target, and needs verbal, somatic components, and a diamond worth at least 300 gold pieces.

parent:326ef7486479381e5449480958207af9d.title: Lifestyle Expenses in D&D
parent:326ef7486479381e5449480958207af9d.summary: Lifestyle expenses in D&D represent the cost of living, ranging from Wretched (free) to Aristocratic (10 GP per day), with each level affecting character exposure to risks and how they are perceived, though these have no inherent consequences unless the GM decides otherwise.

table:e417fb8e02643148fb20683b104c51b6ee.summary: The table lists a condition called 'Squalid' that results in a penalty of 1 Sanity Point per day for being exposed to natural dangers while sleeping outside, as referenced in System Reference Document 5.2.
prose_rows: The 'Squalid' condition, resulting from sleeping outside and exposure to natural dangers, grants 1 spell point per day.

table:d3e78f10d1592020efe44b669c29fbb6ed.summary: The table outlines three spending levels—Poor, Modest, and Comfortable—detailing the daily expenditure and corresponding lifestyle conditions, from minimal spending with potential risks to a more secure and comfortable lifestyle.
prose_rows: Spending the bare minimum for necessities may expose you to unhealthy conditions and opportunistic criminals.
At a poor spending level of 2 SP per day, you spend frugally for your necessities.
With a modest spending level of 1 GP per day, you support yourself at an average level.
At a comfortable spending level of 2 GP per day, you maintain a comfortable lifestyle.

table:1af213855bf26de4386e67b4b43ebf35d3.summary: The table lists spending levels, distinguishing between modest spending with some luxuries and a 'Wealthy' category with 4 GP per day.
prose_rows: A character in the 'Wealthy' category can spend 4 gold pieces per day, covering modest necessities and enjoying a few luxuries.

table:1fa83e8eacb8ec77483f55e39606961307.summary: The table lists the 'Aristocratic' status level with a daily value of 10 GP.
prose_rows: Individuals accustomed to the finer things in life might have servants and receive a daily allowance of 10 gold pieces.

parent:9335878232cc47b0ce289b09236f22477.title: Gargoyle Core Rules and Concepts
parent:9335878232cc47b0ce289b09236f22477.summary: The Gargoyle is a Medium Elemental with high AC and HP, capable of flying and stealth, immune to several conditions, and can perform a Multiattack with two Claw attacks, benefiting from the Flyby trait to avoid Opportunity Attacks.

parent:1fdd220755dc60fcfdcb89e421078ed0b.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:1fdd220755dc60fcfdcb89e421078ed0b.summary: Using higher-level spell slots extends concentration duration, 'Dominate Person' allows telepathic control of a charmed humanoid, 'Dragon’s Breath' enables a creature to exhale damaging energy, and 'Dream' lets a messenger interact with a target's dreams, with damage scaling with spell slot levels above 2.

parent:7f75d6723283a9c8a0e601c46baae06bd.title: Warhorse Core Rules and Concepts
parent:7f75d6723283a9c8a0e601c46baae06bd.summary: A Warhorse is a Large Beast with AC 11, initiative +1, 19 HP, 60 ft. speed, passive perception 11, no languages, CR 1/2, and can attack with hooves causing 9 bludgeoning damage, with extra damage and a prone condition if it charges.

parent:0be83f9877d4b1654601e63cf6fdf90bd.title: Core Rules/Concepts in D&D Rulebook Snippet
parent:0be83f9877d4b1654601e63cf6fdf90bd.summary: Armor Class is determined by base AC plus Dexterity modifier or equipment rules, attack bonuses for weapons depend on proficiency and ability modifiers, spellcasting involves calculating save DC and attack bonuses using ability modifiers and proficiency, and spell management includes tracking spell slots, cantrips, and prepared spells.

parent:efa66306c55d4d68cd9e3dc9591379ef7.title: Troll Core Rules and Concepts
parent:efa66306c55d4d68cd9e3dc9591379ef7.summary: A Troll is a Large Giant with Chaotic Evil alignment, possessing high AC, HP, and speed, with abilities like limb severing, regeneration, and actions including Multiattack and Charge.

parent:f2c057b471ce238863f2bf74c6f86e0cc.title: Sentient Magic Items in D&D
parent:f2c057b471ce238863f2bf74c6f86e0cc.summary: Sentient magic items in D&D have specific goals such as seeking knowledge, protecting certain creatures, finding a soulmate, or defending a deity's interests, and can conflict with their bearers if their actions oppose the item's alignment, leading to demands or control attempts.

parent:0364d297543667b3eb43df9ab67eaef5c.title: Young Brass Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:0364d297543667b3eb43df9ab67eaef5c.summary: The Young Brass Dragon is a large, metallic, chaotic good dragon with AC 17, initiative +3, 110 HP, and speeds of 40 ft., burrow 20 ft., and fly 80 ft., possessing skills in perception, persuasion, and stealth, immunity to fire, blindsight and darkvision, and languages in Common and Draconic, with a challenge rating of 6, capable of multiattacks including rend and breath attacks like fire and sleep breath, which can deal significant damage and incapacitate or render unconscious creatures that fail saving throws.

parent:f353bbe4a0e85665447118f1d2c7aa5fd.title: Werewolf Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f353bbe4a0e85665447118f1d2c7aa5fd.summary: The werewolf is a medium or small monstrosity with chaotic evil alignment, featuring abilities like Pack Tactics, Multiattack, Bite, Scratch, and Longbow, and can shape-shift between forms while maintaining its statistics except for size.

parent:2bdf8621a66dd17de6b595b3e84af2731.title: Young Copper Dragon Summary
parent:2bdf8621a66dd17de6b595b3e84af2731.summary: The Young Copper Dragon is a large, metallic, chaotic good dragon with AC 17, initiative +4, 119 HP, and speeds of 40 ft. on the ground, 40 ft. climbing, and 80 ft. flying, possessing skills in deception, perception, and stealth, immunity to acid, blindsight and darkvision, and the ability to speak Common and Draconic, with a CR of 7, capable of multiattacks including rend and Slowing Breath, and Acid Breath with specific saving throw DCs and damage.

parent:8204e82d2b4fc21ca5452a305640309d0.title: Giant Rat Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8204e82d2b4fc21ca5452a305640309d0.summary: The Giant Rat is a small, unaligned beast with darkvision, capable of climbing and benefiting from Pack Tactics, which grants it advantage on attacks when allies are nearby, and it can bite for 5 piercing damage.

parent:2dd8928782cb1728fe5e2e88466024213.title: Core Rules and Concepts of the Monk Class in D&D
parent:2dd8928782cb1728fe5e2e88466024213.summary: Monks in D&D rely on Dexterity and Wisdom, gain hit points with a D8 die per level, have Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and are proficient in specific skills and weapons, starting with a choice of equipment, and develop martial arts abilities and enhanced movement as they level up.

table:076c807bbf6e96be3f3537fbe36d7192b6.summary: The table lists two options for obtaining tool proficiency: selecting specific items plus an Explorer’s Pack and 11 GP, or paying 50 GP.
prose_rows: The first option includes a dagger, a choice between an artisan's tool or musical instrument for tool proficiency, an explorer's pack, and 11 GP.
The second option is a straightforward 50 GP.

table:88c2525e7ce88294a01702458e0d31157c.summary: The table lists the progression of Monk features, including proficiency bonus, class features, martial arts damage, focus points, and movement speed from levels 1 to 20.
prose_rows: At level 1, Monks gain a +2 proficiency bonus, Martial Arts, Unarmored Defense, and can make a 1d6 Martial Arts check.
At level 2, Monks have a +2 proficiency bonus, gain Monk’s Focus, Unarmored Movement, and Uncanny Metabolism, with a 1d6 Martial Arts check and a +10 ft. movement bonus.
At level 3, Monks have a +2 proficiency bonus, gain Deflect Attacks, Monk Subclass, and a 1d6 Martial Arts check, with a +10 ft. movement bonus.
At level 4, Monks have a +2 proficiency bonus, gain Ability Score Improvement, Slow Fall, and a 1d6 Martial Arts check, with a +10 ft. movement bonus.
At level 5, Monks have a +3 proficiency bonus, gain Extra Attack, Stunning Strike, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +10 ft. movement bonus.
At level 6, Monks have a +3 proficiency bonus, gain Empowered Strikes, Subclass feature, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +15 ft. movement bonus.
At level 7, Monks have a +3 proficiency bonus, gain Evasion, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +15 ft. movement bonus.
At level 8, Monks have a +3 proficiency bonus, gain Ability Score Improvement, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +15 ft. movement bonus.
At level 9, Monks have a +4 proficiency bonus, gain Acrobatic Movement, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +15 ft. movement bonus.
At level 10, Monks have a +4 proficiency bonus, gain Heightened Focus, Self-Restoration, and a 1d8 Martial Arts check, with a +20 ft. movement bonus.
At level 11, Monks have a +4 proficiency bonus, gain a Subclass feature, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +20 ft. movement bonus.
At level 12, Monks have a +4 proficiency bonus, gain Ability Score Improvement, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +20 ft. movement bonus.
At level 13, Monks have a +5 proficiency bonus, gain Deflect Energy, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +20 ft. movement bonus.
At level 14, Monks have a +5 proficiency bonus, gain Disciplined Survivor, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +25 ft. movement bonus.
At level 15, Monks have a +5 proficiency bonus, gain Perfect Focus, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +25 ft. movement bonus.
At level 16, Monks have a +5 proficiency bonus, gain Ability Score Improvement, and a 1d10 Martial Arts check, with a +25 ft. movement bonus.
At level 17, Monks have a +6 proficiency bonus, gain a Subclass feature, and a 1d12 Martial Arts check, with a +25 ft. movement bonus.
At level 18, Monks have a +6 proficiency bonus, gain Superior Defense, and a 1d12 Martial Arts check, with a +30 ft. movement bonus.
At level 19, Monks have a +6 proficiency bonus, gain Epic Boon, and a 1d12 Martial Arts check, with a +30 ft. movement bonus.
At level 20, Monks have a +6 proficiency bonus, gain Body and Mind, and a 1d12 Martial Arts check, with a +30 ft. movement bonus.

parent:439231034592270670a0abf71a05710e7.title: Core Rules/Concepts from D&D Rulebook Snippet
parent:439231034592270670a0abf71a05710e7.summary: The character gains advantage on saving throws against Fiends and Undead, deals Radiant damage to enemies entering the aura, and the aura emits bright sunlight.

parent:1bc4a595d30772b625c1787f2d776621d.title: Gelatinous Cube Core Rules and Concepts
parent:1bc4a595d30772b625c1787f2d776621d.summary: The Gelatinous Cube is a large, unaligned ooze with immunities to several conditions, capable of engulfing creatures to deal Acid damage and impose suffocation and Restrained conditions, while being difficult to notice unless it moves or acts.

parent:55b80c80d9aa61eb3a66042e96b167a55.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:55b80c80d9aa61eb3a66042e96b167a55.summary: The snippet describes spells with diverse effects, including creating sensory phenomena, manipulating nature, causing tremors with potential structural damage, hurling energy beams, and exerting elemental control, each with specific casting requirements and outcomes.

parent:fcbe6912d3e8418ec33b8cd5f30743389.title: Weasel Core Rules/Concepts
parent:fcbe6912d3e8418ec33b8cd5f30743389.summary: The Weasel is a tiny, unaligned beast with high initiative and climbing ability, excelling in acrobatics and stealth, possessing darkvision, and having a low combat challenge rating, making it a minor threat with a simple bite attack.

parent:b15f1ac259bc8577184a5f311a2c45a72.title: Troll Limb Core Rules
parent:b15f1ac259bc8577184a5f311a2c45a72.summary: A Troll Limb is a small, chaotic evil creature with regeneration, transforming into a full troll if not destroyed within 24 hours, and can attack with a rend action causing slashing damage.

parent:e488477c39ee0ac9b8907b94679940aeb.title: Magic Items A–Z
parent:e488477c39ee0ac9b8907b94679940aeb.summary: Magic items in D&D, such as Adamantine Armor, various types of ammunition, and amulets, provide unique benefits like critical hit resistance, attack and damage bonuses, and special abilities like protection against detection or plane shifting, with their effects often tied to item rarity and specific game mechanics.

parent:36bb2cef3f38a2a76447661e11c74b45b.title: Adult Brass Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:36bb2cef3f38a2a76447661e11c74b45b.summary: The Adult Brass Dragon is a large, metallic, chaotic good dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, immune to fire, possessing strong skills and senses, and capable of Multiattack, Fire Breath, Sleep Breath, and Spellcasting, along with Legendary Resistance and Actions.

parent:aff1e39388d0bdedc672a641b1e58038f.title: White Dragon Wyrmling Core Rules and Concepts
parent:aff1e39388d0bdedc672a641b1e58038f.summary: The White Dragon Wyrmling is a Medium-sized, Chaotic Evil Chromatic Dragon with an Armor Class of 16, Initiative of +2, 32 Hit Points, and various movement speeds; it has immunities to Cold, senses including Blindsight and Darkvision, and speaks Draconic; it can traverse icy terrains without penalty, and its actions include a Multiattack with Rend and a Cold Breath attack that deals Cold damage.

parent:dc7f87303653b9b180a7320024b2a2a65.title: Adult Copper Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:dc7f87303653b9b180a7320024b2a2a65.summary: The Adult Copper Dragon is a large, metallic, chaotic good dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, skilled in deception, perception, and stealth, immune to acid, possessing blindsight and darkvision, and speaking Common and Draconic, with a high challenge rating, legendary resistance, and abilities including rend attacks, breath attacks, spellcasting, and legendary actions like Giggling Magic, Mind Jolt, and Pounce.

parent:8802339f2d985d7ca9bfdd75240a3b8a9.title: Giant Scorpion Core Rules
parent:8802339f2d985d7ca9bfdd75240a3b8a9.summary: The Giant Scorpion is a large, unaligned beast with high AC and HP, capable of blindsight and multiattacks involving claws that can grapple and a sting that inflicts piercing and poison damage.

parent:b9ea02a0ddd8506c6cf101314b9e069f3.title: Young Gold Dragon Summary
parent:b9ea02a0ddd8506c6cf101314b9e069f3.summary: The Young Gold Dragon is a large, lawful good metallic dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, capable of flying, swimming, and breathing both air and water, immune to fire, with skills in Insight, Perception, Persuasion, and Stealth, and combat abilities including Rend, Weakening Breath, and Fire Breath, with a CR of 10.

parent:86f582a87cd68c502aabe732dc0de1d4d.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:86f582a87cd68c502aabe732dc0de1d4d.summary: The snippet outlines five character alignments based on morality and order, and provides instructions for character creation, including recording class features, calculating saving throws and skills with proficiency bonuses, and determining passive perception.

parent:c7bcf1faed3bf37f6e5279d182f5e5a12.title: Ghast Core Rules and Concepts
parent:c7bcf1faed3bf37f6e5279d182f5e5a12.summary: The Ghast is a Medium Undead with Chaotic Evil alignment, featuring resistances to Necrotic damage, immunities to several conditions, and abilities like Stench and attacks such as Bite and Claw, which can Paralyze non-Undead creatures.

parent:c6b418f622037f9165ecba9c28a31fb17.title: Core Druid Spellcasting Rules in D&D
parent:c6b418f622037f9165ecba9c28a31fb17.summary: Druids regain spell slots after a Long Rest, prepare a list of level 1+ spells that increases with levels, can change prepared spells post-rest, use Wisdom for spellcasting, and have unique features like Druidic language and Wild Shape, with specific abilities and limitations.

parent:2d6d2f377d157cf3a29934b26a9fae8c4.title: Wolf Creature Summary
parent:2d6d2f377d157cf3a29934b26a9fae8c4.summary: The Wolf is a Medium Beast with AC 12, HP 11, speed 40 ft., and skills in Perception and Stealth, possessing Darkvision and Pack Tactics for combat advantage when allies are nearby, and can bite to deal damage and potentially cause a target to become Prone.

parent:60936386714632721daf157b7c56696a0.title: Legal Information for SRD 5.2
parent:60936386714632721daf157b7c56696a0.summary: The SRD 5.2 is freely available under the CC-BY-4.0 license, requiring attribution to Wizards of the Coast and allowing works to be marked as '5E compatible', with a disclaimer limiting liability.

parent:8096dea5367e39054f2178382521c93a1.title: Unicorn Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8096dea5367e39054f2178382521c93a1.summary: The unicorn is a large celestial creature with high initiative and health, immune to poison and certain conditions, possessing darkvision and telepathy, and capable of resisting magic, casting spells, and performing powerful attacks and legendary actions.

parent:28145608ea1441124dd79d83bb9c1b4b6.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:28145608ea1441124dd79d83bb9c1b4b6.summary: The snippet describes spells that allow detection of magical elements, understanding of languages, compulsion of movement, casting of cold damage, and inducing confusion, each with specific casting requirements and effects.

parent:3bf2f80d92333a5e9aa9ca3fb2e4d086c.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:3bf2f80d92333a5e9aa9ca3fb2e4d086c.summary: The Animated Shield allows a bonus action to animate and protect the user, the Apparatus of the Crab is a legendary vehicle resembling a giant lobster with specific operational mechanics and damage vulnerabilities, and the Armors of Invulnerability and Resistance provide varying levels of damage resistance and immunity, with specific attunement and rarity requirements.

parent:0c17c2669b1a2d8dbfca864d940c8380c.title: Young White Dragon Summary
parent:0c17c2669b1a2d8dbfca864d940c8380c.summary: The Young White Dragon is a large, chaotic evil chromatic dragon with high AC and HP, capable of moving swiftly on various terrains, possessing strong perception and stealth skills, immune to cold, and equipped with abilities like Ice Walk, Multiattack, Rend, and Cold Breath, making it a formidable opponent with a challenge rating of 6.

parent:46ad162bbd025b1f7a1b77f1edd9db003.title: D&D Spell Summary
parent:46ad162bbd025b1f7a1b77f1edd9db003.summary: Hold Person paralyzes a humanoid target, Holy Aura grants saving throw advantages and blinds fiends/undead, Hunter's Mark deals extra damage and aids in tracking, and Hypnotic Pattern charms creatures within a pattern, rendering them incapacitated.

table:b6c71f78b18012bef37366a4d2eb846a93.summary: The table lists a level 8 Abjuration spell for Clerics, with an action casting time, self range, and material components including a reliquary worth 1,000+ GP.
prose_rows: The Level 8 Abjuration spell for a Cleric requires an action to cast, has a range of self, and necessitates verbal, somatic, and material components, with the material component being a reliquary valued at a minimum of 1,000 gold pieces.

parent:c4bef13160372358e2f566b9d3972fa2a.title: Adult Gold Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:c4bef13160372358e2f566b9d3972fa2a.summary: The Adult Gold Dragon is a formidable lawful good creature with high AC, initiative, and HP, capable of flying, swimming, and breathing both air and water, immune to fire, and possessing strong skills in Insight, Perception, Persuasion, and Stealth, with blindsight, darkvision, and communication in Common and Draconic, featuring a high challenge rating, legendary resistance, multiattack with rend and spellcasting, fire breath, weakening breath, and the ability to cast spells like Detect Magic, Guiding Bolt, Shapechange, Flame Strike, and Zone of Truth, along with legendary actions such as Banish, Guiding Light, and Pounce.

parent:59f224e8b08c1b8d3927061093a982cbb.title: Mounts and Vehicles in D&D
parent:59f224e8b08c1b8d3927061093a982cbb.summary: Mounts and vehicles in D&D serve to transport players and their gear, with specific rules for carrying capacities, costs, and equipment like barding and saddles, while large vehicles have additional considerations for speed, crew, and cargo.

table:9019e15112a00b3f1d3f99e71056b4a3fb.summary: The table lists different mounts and animals, specifying their carrying capacities and costs, relevant for riding an aquatic or flying mount.
prose_rows: A camel has a carrying capacity of 450 pounds and costs 50 gold pieces.
An elephant can carry 1,320 pounds and costs 200 gold pieces.
A draft horse has a carrying capacity of 540 pounds and costs 50 gold pieces.
A riding horse can carry 480 pounds and costs 75 gold pieces.
A mastiff has a carrying capacity of 195 pounds and costs 25 gold pieces.
A mule can carry 420 pounds and costs 8 gold pieces.
A pony has a carrying capacity of 225 pounds and costs 30 gold pieces.
A warhorse can carry 540 pounds and costs 400 gold pieces.

table:54343ecde54f89b580761304141dce1118.summary: The table lists the weights and costs of various vehicles and saddles, along with the daily costs for feed and stabling.
prose_rows: A carriage weighs 600 lb and costs 100 GP.
A cart weighs 200 lb and costs 15 GP.
A chariot weighs 100 lb and costs 250 GP.
Feed per day weighs 10 lb and costs 5 CP.
An exotic saddle weighs 40 lb and costs 60 GP.
A military saddle weighs 30 lb and costs 20 GP.
A riding saddle weighs 25 lb and costs 10 GP.
A sled weighs 300 lb and costs 20 GP.
Stabling per day costs 5 SP.
A wagon weighs 400 lb and costs 35 GP.

table:9604e2a2a93f10703ada52a551afa0a48f.summary: The table lists different airborne and waterborne vehicles along with their specifications such as speed, crew, passengers, cargo capacity, armor class, horsepower, damage threshold, and cost.
prose_rows: An airship travels at 8 mph, requires a crew of 10, can carry 20 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 1 ton, an AC of 13, 300 HP, no damage threshold, and costs 40,000 GP.
A galley moves at 4 mph, needs a crew of 80, can carry 150 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 15 tons, an AC of 500, 20 HP, a damage threshold of 20, and costs 30,000 GP.
A keelboat travels at 1 mph, requires a crew of 1, can carry 6.5 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 15 tons, an AC of 100, 10 HP, no damage threshold, and costs 3,000 GP.
A longship moves at 3 mph, needs a crew of 40, can carry 150 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 10 tons, an AC of 300, 15 HP, a damage threshold of 15, and costs 10,000 GP.
A rowboat travels at 1.5 mph, requires a crew of 1, can carry 3 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 11 tons, an AC of 50, no HP, no damage threshold, and costs 50 GP.
A sailing ship moves at 2 mph, needs a crew of 20, can carry 20 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 100 tons, an AC of 300, 15 HP, a damage threshold of 15, and costs 10,000 GP.
A warship travels at 2.5 mph, requires a crew of 60, can carry 60 passengers, has a cargo capacity of 200 tons, an AC of 500, 20 HP, a damage threshold of 20, and costs 25,000 GP.

table:e3d889858dcf7a27ec9758aac2243cee25.summary: The table lists the number of small and medium passengers a ship can accommodate using hammocks, the reduced capacity with private accommodations, and the varying costs for hammocks and private cabins.
prose_rows: The ship can accommodate a certain number of small and medium passengers using hammocks, with private accommodations reducing this capacity to one-fifth.
A passenger typically pays 5 SP per day for a hammock, though prices may vary between ships.
A small private cabin usually costs 2 GP per day.

table:2afca58c3af0cc477ad670682638ae7007.summary: The table outlines the time and cost required to repair a ship's damage while berthed, noting that repairs take 1 day and cost 20 GP per Hit Point, with potential variations in cost and time depending on the availability of supplies and skilled labor.
prose_rows: Repairs to a damaged ship can be made while the vessel is berthed.
Repairing 1 Hit Point of damage requires 1 day and costs 20 GP for materials and labor.
If the repairs are made in a location where supplies and skilled labor are abundant, such as a city, the process may be more efficient.

parent:5728292b8ed647d820dc52e36541dcd0a.title: D&D Spell Mechanics Summary
parent:5728292b8ed647d820dc52e36541dcd0a.summary: The spells 'Chain Lightning,' 'Calm Emotions,' and 'Charm Monster' involve casting actions with specific ranges and components, causing damage or altering conditions, with enhanced effects when using higher-level spell slots.

parent:098ba6d23416afc1398290da1c1bdcbd4.title: Vampire Familiar Core Rules
parent:098ba6d23416afc1398290da1c1bdcbd4.summary: The Vampire Familiar is a Medium or Small Humanoid with AC 15, HP 65, and Speed 30 ft., possessing skills in Perception, Persuasion, and Stealth, resistances to Necrotic damage, and immunities to Charm except from its master, capable of telepathic communication with its vampire master, attacking with Umbral Daggers that cause necrotic damage and paralysis, and using a bonus action for enhanced mobility.

parent:c056d210518fad2b8fb85dcc6a425aac8.title: D&D Spell Preparation Rules
parent:c056d210518fad2b8fb85dcc6a425aac8.summary: In D&D, characters prepare spells based on their class, with specific conditions for changing their spell list, and some spells are always prepared without affecting the list's capacity.

parent:d262ced83dc824e886e977431f988c7cb.title: D&D Rulebook Snippet Summary
parent:d262ced83dc824e886e977431f988c7cb.summary: The snippet outlines the mechanics of cold damage, terrain alteration by hailstones, increased damage from higher-level spell slots, and details of spells like Identify, Illusory Script, and Imprisonment, including their casting requirements, effects, and conditions for success or failure.

table:6ec7c8503e475760fa94a1086497457cc3.summary: The table lists a Level 1 Divination spell for Bards and Wizards, with a casting time of 1 minute or as a ritual, a touch range, and components including verbal, somatic, and a pearl worth at least 100 GP.
prose_rows: The Level 1 Divination spell, available to Bards and Wizards, has a casting time of 1 minute or can be cast as a ritual, requires touch range, and involves verbal, somatic components, and a material component consisting of a pearl worth at least 100 GP.

table:e44db4aad8204684126a54248611cf968f.summary: The table lists a Level 1 Illusion spell for Bards, Warlocks, and Wizards, detailing its casting time, range, and components, including a material component of ink worth at least 10 GP.
prose_rows: The Level 1 Illusion spell, available to Bards, Warlocks, and Wizards, has a casting time of 1 minute or can be cast as a ritual, requires touching the target, and needs somatic and material components, including ink worth at least 10 gold pieces.

table:989aeed124a603b6e1bf64a1f8bc1387e3.summary: The table lists the casting time, range, and components required for a spell, which include verbal and somatic components, and a material component of a statuette worth at least 5,000 GP.
prose_rows: The casting time for the spell is 1 minute.
The spell has a range of 30 feet.
The components required for the spell include verbal (V), somatic (S), and material (M) components, specifically a statuette of the target worth 5,000+ GP.

parent:8ad8e3ce25cbd0f1dc2880a2a65d75283.title: Ancient Gold Dragon Core Rules and Concepts
parent:8ad8e3ce25cbd0f1dc2880a2a65d75283.summary: The Ancient Gold Dragon is a formidable Lawful Good dragon with high AC, initiative, and HP, capable of flying, swimming, and breathing both air and water, immune to fire, and possessing strong skills in Insight, Perception, Persuasion, and Stealth, with blindsight and darkvision, and the ability to communicate in Common and Draconic, featuring a high Challenge Rating, legendary resistance, multiattack with rend and spellcasting, fire breath, weakening breath, and the ability to cast spells like Detect Magic, Guiding Bolt, Shapechange, Flame Strike, Word of Recall, and Zone of Truth, along with legendary actions including Banish, Guiding Light, and Pounce.

parent:f98d0fc6a6249f13e772e61669d2dabdc.title: Wraith Core Rules and Concepts
parent:f98d0fc6a6249f13e772e61669d2dabdc.summary: A Wraith is a Medium or Small Undead with high AC, initiative, and HP, resistances to multiple damage types, immunities to various conditions, and abilities like incorporeal movement, sunlight sensitivity, Life Drain, and Create Specter, allowing it to control specters.

parent:2b505e862af7fe2b647b66b5d3cb38001.title: D&D Magical Items Summary
parent:2b505e862af7fe2b647b66b5d3cb38001.summary: The Belt of Giant Strength increases a character's strength based on its rarity, the Berserker Axe offers bonuses but curses the user, and the Boots of Elvenkind, Levitation, Speed, and Striding and Springing provide various movement and stealth advantages.

parent:67d2da7df29dcc4ef676798de43ca225d.title: Summary of D&D Rulebook Snippet
parent:67d2da7df29dcc4ef676798de43ca225d.summary: The snippet describes magical items and weapons with unique abilities, such as truesight, extra damage against giants, illusionary armor, missile snaring, enhanced climbing and swimming, night vision, and a legendary hammer with thunderbolt attacks, each providing specific bonuses and effects.

parent:c70d4348d863a0379aff1fd2eb36b416a.title: Axe Beak
parent:c70d4348d863a0379aff1fd2eb36b416a.summary: The Axe Beak is a large, unaligned monstrosity with an AC of 11, initiative +1, 19 HP, 50 ft. speed, passive perception of 10, no languages, a CR of 1/4, and a beak attack that deals 6 slashing damage on a successful hit.

parent:03a411933d16775a85ef7da990a70e86d.title: Vampire Spawn Summary
parent:03a411933d16775a85ef7da990a70e86d.summary: The Vampire Spawn is a Medium or Small Undead creature with AC 16, HP 90, and Speed 30 ft., possessing skills in Perception and Stealth, resistances to Necrotic damage, and senses including Darkvision; it speaks Common and one other language, has a CR of 5, and features traits like Spider Climb and weaknesses such as Forbiddance, Running Water, Stake to the Heart, and Sunlight, with actions including Multiattack, Claw, and Bite, and a bonus action called Deathless Agility.

parent:cec80d42c254e55d9b984bc08d48fbd0a.title: Core Rules for the Wizard Class in D&D
parent:cec80d42c254e55d9b984bc08d48fbd0a.summary: Wizards primarily use Intelligence for spellcasting, gain proficiency in skills like Arcana and History, and start with simple weapons and no armor; they learn spells at level 1, with increasing features and spell slots at higher levels, and can replace cantrips after a long rest.

table:d15af80797b69cce782429c42abf23b018.summary: The table lists two starting equipment options: Option A with specific items and 5 GP, or Option B with 55 GP.
prose_rows: Option A for starting equipment includes 2 daggers, an arcane focus (quarterstaff), a robe, a spellbook, a scholar’s pack, and 5 gold pieces.
Option B for starting equipment provides 55 gold pieces.
